title: The superwind galaxy NGC 4666
caption: The starburst galaxy NGC 4666, imaged by the MPG/ESO 2.2-meter telescope at La Silla, Chile
celestial: NGC 4666 · constellation Virgo · about 80 million light-years away (source figure)

recognition.text: Official ESO press-release image. No published audience rating.

story: This visible-light image shows the galaxy NGC 4666 at its center, with its neighbor NGC 4668 visible to the lower left. Lying around 80 million light-years from Earth, NGC 4666 is a starburst galaxy, where especially intense star formation is under way. The picture comes from the Wide Field Imager, a camera on the MPG/ESO 2.2-meter telescope at ESO's La Silla Observatory in Chile.

The starburst is thought to have been set off by gravitational interactions with neighboring galaxies, NGC 4668 among them. Supernova explosions and powerful winds from massive stars in the starburst region together push an immense stream of gas out of the galaxy and into space, an outflow known as a superwind.

ESA's XMM-Newton space telescope had earlier observed NGC 4666 in X-rays. These visible-light observations were made to follow up background objects spotted in those X-ray images. The field covers 16 by 12 arcminutes and combines twelve CCD frames of 67 megapixels each, shot through filters for blue, green and red light.
scale: Using the source's listed field of view (15.64 x 12.55 arcminutes) and distance (80 million light years), the frame spans roughly 364,000 × 292,000 light-years. Its light set out about 80 million years before reaching the telescope.

understand.summary: The Wide Field Imager recorded visible light through blue, green and red filters. The color mapping isn't published.
understand.eye: Long camera exposures gather more light than the eye can.
